title: Rollback fencing failure during model shard resync
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Summary: During a staged rollout of model v2026-02b we attempted a rollback after elevated 5xxs were observed in EU region. The rollback request overlapped with an ongoing model shard resync (metadata and KV cache reconciliation) on a subset of serving racks. A fencing check that prevents concurrent conflicting route state changes failed to assert, allowing a partial rollforward/rollback interleaving. This resulted in ~18 minutes of dual-serve (some requests hit v2026-02b, some hit v2026-01f) with mismatched KV cache states, causing inconsistent responses, increased token retries, and a spike in downstream error rates for customers with model-version pins. Estimated affected requests: ~140k; impact window: 18m.
timeline: 2026-02-17T21:42:00Z - Monitoring alert: EU 5xx rate > 3x baseline for model v2026-02b (top error: missing-kv-key)
2026-02-17T21:47:00Z - PM & on-call Eng convene; decision to initiate rollback to v2026-01f for EU canary (20% subset)
2026-02-17T21:48:30Z - Rollback API call triggered by orchestrator; rollback enters pending state while resync runs
2026-02-17T21:49:10Z - Orchestrator starts shard resync for region EU to reconcile metadata and KV cache (expected duration ~12m)
2026-02-17T21:50:05Z - Fencing check (fence token acquisition) fails intermittently due to a leader-change race in orchestrator; no hard abort invoked
2026-02-17T21:51:00Z - Partial rollout controller applies route deltas to subset of racks (some racks switch back to v2026-01f while others continue serving v2026-02b)
2026-02-17T22:05:30Z - Customer reports increase in malformed/partial JSON outputs for pinned-model requests; incidence escalates
2026-02-17T22:10:30Z - KV cache invalidation mismatch observed: some workers lacking updated prefix cache for v2026-01f return missing-kv-key errors
2026-02-17T22:20:30Z - Orchestrator completes resync; fence tokens reconcile but state already diverged (dual-serve continues)
2026-02-17T22:30:00Z - Manual operator intervention to force-quiesce route table and perform an ordered rollback across all racks
2026-02-17T22:36:00Z - All racks confirmed serving v2026-01f with consistent KV cache; error rate returns to baseline
2026-02-17T22:40:00Z - Post-incident triage meeting scheduled; on-call writes preliminary incident notes
impact_summary: Users with model-version pins and cross-region fallbacks experienced inconsistent responses and elevated error rates for approximately 18 minutes. Several enterprise customers reported degraded inference quality and increased retries. No secrets or customer data were exposed; the impact was availability/consistency only. Estimated customer-affecting requests: ~140k. SLA credit likely required for impacted Dedicated customers.
root_cause: A race between the orchestrator leader election and the rollback fencing logic allowed conflicting route updates during an ongoing shard resync. The fencing logic assumed atomic token acquisition but did not account for transient leadership handoffs; as a result, rollback deltas were applied to some racks before KV caches and metadata were reconciled cluster-wide. Additionally, rollback operations were not idempotent at the route-application layer, leading to partial state application.
mitigations: Immediate: Manual ordered rollback and quiesce of route controllers for EU region to restore consistent state
Short-term: Add a temporary global rollback lock for rollbacks that overlap with shard resyncs (config flag rollout)
Short-term: Update monitoring to surface 'fence acquisition failures' as high-priority alerts tied to rollout events
Medium-term: Make route apply idempotent and add strong lease semantics for fencing tokens (prevent application during leadership transitions)
Medium-term: Add precondition check in rollout planner to block rollbacks while resyncs are in progress or to gate route diffs until KV reconciliation completes
Long-term: Improve canary scheduling to avoid overlapping maintenance (resync) and control plane operations; implement safe-rollback dry-run that simulates KV cache reconciliation impact
action_items: ENG-71006 - Implement strong lease-based fencing for route operations (owner: Miguel Santos, estimate: 8)
ENG-71007 - Make route apply idempotent and add transactional commit with rollback compensation (owner: Priya Rao, estimate: 13)
ENG-71008 - Add rollout precondition to block rollbacks during active shard resyncs (owner: Linh Tran, estimate: 5)
ENG-71009 - Create alerting rule and dashboard for fence-token acquisition failures and correlated resyncs (owner: Marco DeLuca, estimate: 3)
ENG-71010 - Backfill canary scheduling policy to not schedule resyncs during planned rollouts; add documentation in Runbook (owner: TD - SRE, estimate: 2)
